title: Make, track and close one realistic promise

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A promise has a recipient, deliverable and deadline. Tracking supports action; a private calendar edit changes none of the recipient’s expectations. A renegotiation needs an actual response or an established alternative procedure.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: On Monday Jo promises a two-paragraph room notice by Thursday 16:00. Drafting takes 20 minutes; Jo has Thursday 15:00–15:30. The room owner must confirm the room name. Wednesday 12:00 reminder reveals no reply. Jo may send an accurate draft with room marked pending, but final publication needs confirmation.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write the commitment and early-check decision. Draft a status request that identifies the unresolved dependency and proposes a bounded alternative without assuming agreement.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A recipient has not answered a request to move Friday’s deadline to Monday. Which deadline is currently agreed?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Jo should contact the owner before the deadline and preserve the pending room. Later fiction: owner agrees Wednesday 17:00 to a draft Thursday 16:00 and final Friday 10:00; room arrives Thursday 18:00. The change is agreed, but neither draft nor final is performed merely by agreement. Partial: set a reminder without reviewing dependency. Incorrect: silently move the deadline or invent the room.
criteria: The commitment has an explicit boundary
Proposed, agreed and performed states differ

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Friday remains the known agreement. Communicate actual risk, use any legitimate escalation route and record an unresolved request; silence is not acceptance.
